title: WHIP Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: WHIP Calculator: Calculate walks plus hits per inning pitched. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Calculate walks plus hits per inning pitched. Enter your walks, hits and innings pitched and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Calculate walks plus hits per inning pitched. This free online whip calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the WHIP Calculator

Start by entering your walks, then entering your hits and finally entering your innings pitched. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your walks.
2. Enter your hits.
3. Enter your innings pitched.
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

WHIP = (walks + hits) ÷ innings pitched.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 40 walks and 120 hits over 150 innings gives 1.067 WHIP. Try the same figures in the [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

With the default values (Walks: 40, Hits: 120, Innings pitched: 150), the [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) returns WHIP: 1.067. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this whip calculator free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the WHIP Calculator use?

WHIP = (walks + hits) ÷ innings pitched. You can see it in action in the [WHIP Calculator](/whip-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the WHIP Calculator?

Just Walks, Hits and Innings pitched. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
